title: Patient Financial Services Terms for Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program Balances
content:
Patient Financial Services terms governing the customer's balance on a Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program.

## 1. The balance

The customer's balance on the program is the running total of its patient-balance postings: remittance patient responsibility, patient charges and refunds add to it, and payments and balance adjustments reduce it; a payment is applied to the oldest unpaid posting first. A balance below zero is a credit balance.

## 2. Balance adjustments

A balance adjustment is posted only for one of these reasons, each against the one posting it adjusts and never for more than that posting's unpaid remainder:

| Reason | Posted for |
|---|---|
| Return credit | An accepted self-pay return, for the price paid for the returned units less the tier's restocking fee percent |
| Secondary payer payment | The amount a secondary payer paid against a remittance's patient responsibility |
| Hardship waiver | Postings named on an approved hardship application, on the conditions of section 3 |
| Small-balance write-off | The program's whole remaining balance, on the conditions of section 4 |
| Billing correction | A posting made in error, or a timely-filing write-off |

## 3. Hardship waiver

A hardship waiver is granted only on tiers where a hardship waiver is allowed, only for postings named on a hardship application whose request status is approved, and only after Larkfield's financial counseling team confirms household income at or below the tier's hardship income ceiling, as a percent of the HHS poverty guideline; it is never granted routinely, never advertised and never granted on the customer's statement alone.

## 4. Small-balance write-off

A small-balance write-off is made only when the whole remaining balance of the program is greater than 0.00 and no more than the tier's small-balance write-off ceiling; on tiers where that ceiling is 0.00 no write-off is made and the balance is statemented.

| Whole remaining balance, ceiling 4.99 USD (hypothetical tier) | Write-off |
|---|---|
| 0.00 USD | No, the balance must be greater than 0.00 |
| 4.99 USD | Yes, the balance is no more than the ceiling |
| 5.00 USD | No |

## 5. Credit balances

A credit balance is refunded to the original payment method no later than the tier's credit-balance refund limit (calendar days) after the posting date of the entry that created it, unless the customer asks in writing to keep it on account; a refund never exceeds the credit.

## 6. Payment plans

*Retired clause.* As originally written, this section provided that a payment plan is offered only on tiers where the longest payment plan is greater than 0 installments, for a balance of at least the tier's payment plan minimum balance, in no more than the tier's longest payment plan of monthly installments of at least the tier's payment plan minimum installment; that it is created as a payment plan request the customer accepts; and that while an approved plan's installments are current the balance it covers is left out of the past-due test. That wording, standing alone, is **no longer in force**. It is superseded by the current basis, which keeps every one of those terms and adds that, for a plan priced under the rule for payment plan installments, and only for such a plan, the balance it covers is the plan balance that rule counts, while every other plan covers the program's own balance.

superseded_clauses: A payment plan is offered only on tiers where payment_plan_max_months is greater than 0, for a balance of at least payment_plan_min_balance_usd, in no more than payment_plan_max_months monthly installments of at least payment_plan_min_monthly_usd; it is created as a payment plan request the customer accepts, and while an approved plan's installments are current the balance it covers is left out of the past-due test measured by cgm_msr_past_due_amount.
